faq_h2: School and Gymnasium Steel Building Questions
faq: Can a steel building be used for a school?

Yes. Pre-engineered steel buildings are used for private, charter, and public schools. We work with your architect to plan the layout, and the building must meet the code requirements for its use. Check with your local building department.
Can you build a steel gymnasium?
Yes. Steel framing allows the wide, column-free span and tall eaves a gymnasium needs. Tell us the sports and seating you plan for so we can design the width, length, and height around them.
Yes. We work closely with your architect so the interior layout fits your school size and planned activities. Share your plans early so the steel building can be designed around them.
Can steel buildings be used for churches?
Yes. Steel buildings can provide sanctuaries, fellowship halls, and multipurpose space. Tell us your layout and seating needs and we will plan the building around them.
Do you supply overhead doors, windows, or interior finishes?

No. We design the building and its openings for the overhead doors and windows you choose, and they are installed by others. We supply commercial walk doors (man doors). Interior finishes are by others.
Yes. We supply insulation. Tell us how you will use the space and we will include the right options in your quote.
Do I need a permit for a school or gymnasium?

Yes, in most places. Requirements vary by county or city and by how the building will be used. Check with your local building department. Your building is engineered for local codes, with plans prepared for permitting.
How long does it take to get a school or gymnasium building?
Our current turnaround is 8 to 10 weeks. Timelines can vary with project size, options, and demand.
